robot.name: NAO
robot.status_notes: NAO V6 is actively sold by RobotLAB and Generation Robots in 2026. The robot's original manufacturer Aldebaran filed for bankruptcy in 2025 and its core assets, including Nao, were acquired by Maxvision Technology Corp. Long-term support depends on Maxvision. No discontinuation of NAO V6 was found.

height.notes: RobotLAB lists 574 mm (about 58 cm). Generation Robots lists 58 cm. Old NAO book lists 57.3 cm; USC page lists 66 cm but that likely includes a different measurement. Official reseller value used.

weight.notes: RobotLAB lists 5.48 kg. Generation Robots lists 5.6 kg. Old book lists <4.3 kg for earlier NAO version.

payload.notes: No payload or carrying capacity was found in the reviewed sources.

runtime.original_value: ~60 min active use, ~90 min normal use
runtime.notes: 60-90 minutes depending on use; conservative lower bound of 1 hour used. Recharge time about 90 minutes per RobotLAB.

battery.notes: RobotLAB and Generation Robots list the same 62.5 Wh battery for NAO V6.

degrees_of_freedom.notes: Manufacturer figure is 25 DoF for NAO V6. RobotLAB notes a tech sheet joint breakdown lists 26; USC page says 26 DoF for NAO H25 V4.0. This pack uses 25, the manufacturer/reseller spec.

walking_speed.notes: No walking speed was found in any reviewed source.

hands.description: Hands have tactile sensors (capacitive); no separate hand degrees of freedom, force feedback, or grip specifications were found.

items: Tactile sensors: head, hands, feet (capacitive + bumpers)
RGB LEDs for eyes, chest button, feet

compute.description: Intel Atom E3845 1.91 GHz CPU, 4 GB DDR3 RAM, 32 GB eMMC storage, NAOqi OS (Gentoo-based Linux).

actuators.description: Maxon coreless DC motors; 25 joint actuators.

availability.notes: RobotLAB sells NAO V6 Standard Edition for $16,990 with lease/RaaS options. Generation Robots lists €10,020 VAT inclusive (€8,350 ex VAT). 1-year warranty via RobotLAB, 2-year warranty via Generation Robots.

manipulation_dexterity.summary: NAO V6 has 25 DoF for full-body gestures, walking, and general motion control; hands have capacitive touch sensors but no separate hand DoF or grasping demos were found. Source1 claims NAO performs full-body gestures and dance; Source5 states the 25 joints enable walking and general motion control. No fine manipulation or gripper demonstrations were found.
caveats: No hand degrees of freedom, force feedback, or payload specification found.
No manipulation demo or success rate in reviewed sources.

autonomy_task_execution.summary: Reseller descriptions and the ResearchGate figure caption describe NAO as autonomous and fully programmable. Source6 describes a study where NAO autonomously instructed a human in a modified Box and Blocks test using verbal commands and head-tap progress input. Several video titles from 2009-2024 suggest autonomous behaviors, but no transcripts were reviewed.
caveats: Autonomy claims are reseller/manufacturer assertions, not independently benchmarked.
Source6 is a single constrained research task, not general autonomy.
Video titles only; actual autonomous behavior was not reviewed.

mobility_whole_body_control.summary: NAO is a true bipedal humanoid that walks, balances, recovers from falls, and performs full-body gestures per RobotLAB FAQ. It has 25 joints designed for walking and general motion control. Video titles from Aldebaran and others show NAO demos, but no transcript was available to confirm gait performance. No walking speed or stability metrics found.
caveats: No walking speed, fall rate, or gait quality measured.
Video evidence is title-only; not verified by manual review.

perception_scene_understanding.summary: NAO V6 includes two 5 MP cameras, four microphones, sonar, IMU, force sensors, and tactile sensors. RobotLAB claims NAO can recognize faces and objects; Generation Robots lists voice recognition, computer vision, and distance sensing. No third-party perception benchmark was found.
caveats: Perception capabilities are product-page claims, not independently evaluated.
No object recognition accuracy or latency data found.

human_interaction.summary: NAO is designed for human-robot interaction: 20+ spoken languages, expressive RGB LEDs, touch sensors, and speech/camera-based interaction. RobotLAB describes use in special education and autism support with consistent, low-anxiety engagement. Source6 is a peer-reviewed study where NAO instructed a human participant and recorded progress, demonstrating HRI use.
caveats: Source6 is one controlled task, not a broad HRI evaluation.
Special-education benefits are reseller claims, not clinical evidence.

endurance_reliability.summary: NAO V6 battery is 62.5 Wh with 60-90 minutes runtime per charge and about 90 minutes recharge. Generation Robots performs pre-shipment functional checks. No long-duration reliability, mean time between failures, or fall recovery rate data was found.
caveats: Short battery life limits continuous operation.
No independent reliability data or failure rates.

human_environment_fit.summary: NAO is 58 cm tall, 5.48-5.6 kg, designed with curved white surfaces and short stature to be non-threatening per The Robot Report. It is used in classrooms, labs, and assistive education. No safety certification for the full robot was found.
caveats: No full-robot safety certification or injury risk data found.
Small size limits physical tasks but improves proximity safety.

deployment_commercial_proof.summary: Aldebaran reportedly sold about 20,000 Nao robots in 70 countries; Generation Robots repeats the same deployment figure. USC Robotics Research Lab is a named academic lab with 12 NAO units. RobotLAB actively sells and leases NAO V6. No commercial industrial deployment with output metrics was found.
caveats: Sales figures are company/reseller claims, not audited.
Named deployment is academic research, not commercial production.
No operating hours or output metrics available.

accessibility_value.summary: NAO V6 is purchasable from RobotLAB for $16,990 and from Generation Robots for €10,020 incl VAT. Lease/RaaS and financing are available. A 2-year warranty is offered by Generation Robots and 1-year by RobotLAB. Short battery life and older Intel Atom compute may limit value for heavy autonomy workloads.
caveats: No OEM direct sales path confirmed; resellers only.
Post-bankruptcy support from Maxvision is not yet proven.

evidence_items.title: NAO V6 RobotLAB product page specifications
evidence_items.claim: RobotLAB lists NAO V6 as 574 mm tall, 5.48 kg, 25 DoF, Intel Atom E3845, 4 GB RAM, 32 GB storage, two 5 MP cameras, Li-ion 62.5 Wh battery, and ~60-90 min runtime.
evidence_items.notes: Reseller product page; official SoftBank/Aldebaran specs not independently measured.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Defines size, compute, sensors, and runtime for comparison.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: NAO V6 stands 574 mm tall, weighs about 5.48 kg, and has 25 degrees of freedom.
evidence_items.source_location: RobotLAB NAO V6 page, FAQ question 2 answer
evidence_items.verification_notes: Company/reseller spec page. DoF conflict noted on same page.

evidence_items.title: NAO V6 walking and balance claim
evidence_items.claim: RobotLAB states NAO is a true bipedal humanoid that walks, balances, recovers from falls, and performs full-body gestures using its 25 joints.
evidence_items.notes: Reseller claim; no video or measured gait evidence reviewed here.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Basis for bipedal mobility and whole-body control scoring.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Yes — unlike wheeled social robots such as Pepper and ARI, NAO is a true bipedal humanoid that walks, balances, recovers from falls, and performs full-body gestures using its 25 joints.
evidence_items.source_location: RobotLAB NAO V6 page, FAQ question 7 answer
evidence_items.verification_notes: Company/reseller claim; no fall recovery metrics.

evidence_items.title: NAO V6 price and purchase options
evidence_items.claim: RobotLAB sells the NAO V6 Standard Edition for $16,990, including robot, charger, battery, Choregraphe Unlimited license, SDK/API, curriculum, warranty, and support.
evidence_items.notes: Reseller price; no OEM direct price found.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: RobotLAB sells the NAO V6 Standard Edition for $16,990, which includes the robot, charger and battery, a Choregraphe Unlimited software license, the full SDK and API, SoftBank curriculum, a one-year warranty, and US-based RobotLAB Support Level 1.

evidence_items.source_location: Generation Robots NAO V6 page, introductory sentence

evidence_items.title: Aldebaran sales figures and Maxvision acquisition
evidence_items.claim: The Robot Report reports Aldebaran sold about 20,000 Nao robots and 17,000 Pepper humanoids to 70 countries; Maxvision acquired Aldebaran's core assets including Nao and Pepper.
evidence_items.notes: Reputable media reporting company statements; sales figures not audited.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Provides broad deployment and corporate context.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: The company said it had sold about 20,000 Nao robots and 17,000 Pepper humanoids to 70 countries, but it stopped producing Pepper in 2020 or 2021.
evidence_items.source_location: The Robot Report article, paragraph about Aldebaran sales
evidence_items.verification_notes: Secondary media summary of Aldebaran claim.

evidence_items.claim: An old NAO book states NAO is 57.3 cm tall, 27.3 cm wide, weighs less than 4.3 kg, and has a 21.6V 2Ah lithium-ion battery for up to 90 minutes.
evidence_items.notes: Historical early-version specs; do not apply to V6.

evidence_items.title: NAO 25 joints for walking and motion control
evidence_items.claim: The NAO humanoid consists of 25 joints that enable walking and general motion control.
evidence_items.notes: Book statement, consistent with manufacturer spec.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Humanoid NAO consists of 25 joints that make walking and general motion control possible.

evidence_items.title: Research use of NAO to instruct and evaluate task switching
evidence_items.claim: A ResearchGate publication describes using NAO to give instructions to a human performing a modified Box and Blocks test, with the robot recording progress via head taps.
evidence_items.notes: Peer-reviewed research result demonstrating an HRI application with NAO executing its role.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Quantified but narrow evidence for autonomous instruction and human interaction.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: The Nao Humanoid Robot [9], Figure 2, was used to give instructions to user while performing the task.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Study appears to be about human task switching, not robot manipulation; robot acts as instructor.

evidence_items.claim: The USC Robotics Research Lab currently has 12 NAO robots, 10 of which are NAO H25 V4.0.

researcher_notes.short_verdict_for_arena: NAO V6 is a purchasable, long-established 58 cm bipedal research/education humanoid with 25 DoF, 5 MP cameras, and 60-90 minute battery life. Strongest evidence is actual market availability and broad deployment claims (20,000 units in 70 countries) plus a named USC lab fleet. However, most capability claims come from reseller spec pages and demo video titles only; no independent autonomy, manipulation, or reliability benchmark was found.
strongest_positive_evidence: Purchasable from RobotLAB ($16,990) and Generation Robots (€10,020 incl VAT) with lease options.
About 20,000 NAO units sold in 70 countries per Aldebaran/media.
USC Robotics Research Lab has 12 NAO units.
Peer-reviewed research study used NAO to instruct a human in a task (Source6).
weakest_or_missing_evidence: No walking speed or payload specification found.
No independent autonomy or reliability benchmark.
Video demos are title-only and not reviewed.
conflicting_claims: DoF: 25 (manufacturer/reseller) vs 26 (RobotLAB tech sheet note and USC page).
Height: 574 mm / 58 cm (RobotLAB, Generation Robots) vs 57.3 cm (old NAO book) vs 66 cm (USC page).
Weight: 5.48 kg (RobotLAB) vs 5.6 kg (Generation Robots) vs <4.3 kg (old book).
Battery: 62.5 Wh V6 vs 2 Ah old book; runtime 60-90 min consistent.
do_not_overclaim: Do not credit specific capabilities from video titles without watching the videos.
Do not apply old NAO V4/V5 specs to V6.
Do not treat the 20,000-unit sales figure as independently audited.
Do not infer hand dexterity, payload, or walking speed from the available specs.
Do not call the USC deployment a commercial industrial proof.

currentness.currentness_notes: NAO V6 is current and purchasable as of 2026-10-29. The original manufacturer Aldebaran entered receivership in 2025 and assets were acquired by Maxvision; resellers continue to list V6 as in active production. No newer NAO model was identified in the sources.

arena_prompt_summary.one_paragraph_summary: NAO V6 is a 58 cm, 5.48 kg, 25-DoF bipedal humanoid sold by RobotLAB for $16,990 and Generation Robots for €10,020 incl VAT. It uses an Intel Atom E3845 with 4 GB RAM, two 5 MP cameras, four microphones, sonar, tactile sensors, and a 62.5 Wh battery rated for 60-90 minutes. About 20,000 units have reportedly been sold in 70 countries; USC has 12 units. It is an education/research platform with Choregraphe, Python, and C++. Autonomy is claimed but not independently benchmarked; video demos exist but were title-only in this review. No payload, walking speed, hand DoF, or manipulation demos were found.
strongest_evidence: Purchasable with price and lease options from two resellers.
Named USC lab with 12 NAO units.
Peer-reviewed research study using NAO to instruct a human task.
weakest_evidence: No independent autonomy or reliability benchmark.
No walking speed, payload, or manipulation demonstration.
Video evidence is title-only and not reviewed.
known_do_not_credit: Old NAO V4/V5 specs as V6.
Specific capabilities from video titles without watching.
Hand dexterity, payload, or walking speed claims.
